o.text: Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kē(y)t- (“to go (away), to get away”). Compare Turkish gitmek.

From Proto-Turkic *kiāl-mak (“to stay behind, remain”).
Cognates
Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰴𐰞 (qal-, “to be left (behind)”), Old Uyghur [script needed] (qal-, “to remain”), Karakhanid قَلْماقْ (qalmāq, “to remain”), Turkish kalmak (“to remain, stay”), Bashkir ҡалыу (qalıw, “to remain”), Chagatai [script needed] (qalmaq, “to remain”), Chuvash юлма (julma, “to remain”), Kazakh қалу (qaluw, “to remain”), Khakas халарға (xalarğa, “to remain”), Kipchak [Arabic needed] (qal-, “to remain, stay”), Kyrgyz калуу (kaluu, “to remain”), Tatar калу (qalu, “to remain”), Turkmen gālmak (“to remain”), Tuvan калыр (kalır, “to remain, stay”), Uyghur قالماق (qalmaq, “to remain”), Uzbek qolmoq (“to remain, stay”), Yakut хаал (qaal, “to remain, stay”).
Likely a calque of Russian и́мени (ímeni).
